newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT-Coffee due higher, consolidation possible.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-Coffee due higher, consolidation possible.

text.p: JULY Close * Support * Resist * RSI14 * MA10 * MA30
Robusta coffee futures were again called to open sharply up on Wednesday after New York ended a bout of profit-taking, but technical analysts said prices might consolidate before the next rally.
Traders called the market to open as much as $170 higher than Tuesday's close after the arabicas market again rose on supply concerns.
But the higher call was based on a theoretical calculation after the New York close, they said, adding that while London would open higher, it might be by only half that amount.

In an extremely volatile session, July erased early gains and slid nearly 5.00 cents/lb. But a late round of commercial buying drove prices higher, driving July up to end at 264.20 cents, up 10.25 cents on the day.
Technical analysts said the London market was building up a good support base as profits were taken after the recent dizzy rallies.

"It's finding quite decent support at the bottom of that end-May range and, providing that level holds, it's got a reasonable chance of going sideways and probably going up again," said Susan Rigg, a technical analyst at Chart Analysis.
"It did have quite a good bounce off that level," she said, referring to a band of trading between $2,030 and $2,050 from the middle of last month.
If prices were to fall through that immediate area of support, then the bottom of a chart gap at $1,940 would be the next target, followed by $1,800.
The upside, by contrast, presented a very ragged picture on the chart and represented a very volatile trading area, Rigg said.
Brazil is now of paramount interest to the market as it enters this year's frost season.
According to independent weather forecaster Weather Services Corporation, Brazil's coffee regions can expect temperatures near to below normal.
The outlook is for mild temperatures on Friday and cooler weather at the weekend. No damaging frost is forecast, but the colder weather this weekend bears watching, WSC said.
